Apex Hosting is dedicated to supporting education and the positive impact of Minecraft in learning. We are excited to offer a scholarship for students passionate about this unique educational tool.
Must be a United States citizen
Must currently be enrolled in high school or college
Submit an essay (minimum 500 words) alongside your academic details.
The scholarship committee will review applications and notify scholarship winners via email.

Minecraft has been used in many different facets of education and we want to know how you believe that the game can be further utilized to enhance learning and development. We are interested in hearing your thoughts and experiences about how this amazing game that we love can be much more than just a game.

The member companies of The Transformer Association (TTA) have established an academic scholarship program for the coming academic year to support qualified students enrolled in degree programs who have exhibited an interest in transformers or power conversion design through course work or other activities, and who might be considering a career in the transformer industry.
Includes an expense-paid trip to the TTA Annual Meeting
Must be enrolled full-time at an undergraduate or graduate student in North America
Must be pursuing a degree in electrical engineering, mechanical engineering, magnetics, transformer design, or a related field
Must demonstrate interest in transformers or power conversion through coursework or experience
Prepare a resume including academic and extracurricular details.
Write a letter describing your interest and experience in transformer-related fields.
Obtain a letter of recommendation from a professor or academic advisor.

TTA will award a scholarship based on academic merit and the applicant’s demonstrated experience and interest in the field of power conversion. The scholarship will be awarded in the form of a one-time grant of $2,500, based on the review of applications and the judgment of the TTA Scholarship Committee and Board of Directors.

Each year the Mahoney Family Foundation awards scholarships to deserving professionals. Grants of up to $5,000 per individual are designed to help offset the financial burden of required Continuing Education Units or Advanced Degrees incurred by our Nurses and Teachers.

Submit documentation of your enrollment in a CEU program or advanced degree.

Submit any additional required documents by the stated deadline.
The Mahoney Family Foundation is a 501c3 organization created to support the ongoing education and training of those in the Nursing and Teaching professions through scholarship programs.

The USRA Distinguished Undergraduate Awards provide college scholarship awards to students who have shown a career interest in science or engineering with an emphasis on space research or space science education, and aeronautics-related sciences.
Sponsored by the Universities Space Research Association (USRA)
Up to five scholarships are awarded annually
Each scholarship provides a one-time award of $5,000
Scholarships recognize students pursuing careers in science, engineering, space research, space science education, and aeronautics-related fields
Scholarships are awarded during the fall academic term
Available memorial scholarships include the Thomas R. McGetchin, John R. Sevier, James B. Willett, Frederick A. Tarantino, and Judith L. Pipher Memorial Scholarship Awards
Must be enrolled full-time at an accredited four-year college or university
Must be pursuing a bachelor's degree in science, engineering, life sciences, science education, or a related field
Must be within two years of earning a Bachelor of Science or Bachelor of Arts degree when the scholarship is awarded
Must demonstrate an interest in science or engineering with an emphasis on space research, space science education, or aeronautics-related sciences
Must satisfy all application requirements established by USRA
Complete the Distinguished Undergraduate Awards application during the summer application period
Prepare and submit all required supporting documentation
Provide information demonstrating your academic achievements and career interests in science or engineering
Submit the completed application before the published deadline
Monitor communications regarding scholarship review and fall award announcements

USRA presents up to five scholarship awards to undergraduate students each fall as part of its Distinguished Undergraduate Award program. Students will be matched to the scholarship most appropriate for their area of study.
Intuitive Digital Inclusion In Digital Marketing Scholarship

We are proud to continue to offer a scholarship for one deserving student. While this year’s amount is a little smaller than last year's, our commitment hasn’t changed. The world feels uncertain these days, so it’s even more important that we continue what we’re doing and keep showing up and investing in a more inclusive future for marketing.
$2,500 one-time award for the upcomimg academic year
Open until 200 applications are received or August 15th, whichever comes first
Winner announced by end of August; funds distributed in September
May be used for undergraduate tuition, fees, books, or program-related equipment
Past recipients may reapply in subsequent years if still eligible
Undergraduate entering junior or senior year in the coming Fall
Declared major in digital marketing, communications, UX, graphic design, web development, or business with plans to open a digital agency
Enrolled at least half-time in an accredited U.S. four-year college or university
Proof of enrollment and declared area of study required
Preference for applicants from underrepresented groups (e.g., African-American, Hispanic/Latinx, Native American, Pacific Islander, Asian, LGBTQIA+, women, nonbinary, gender non-conforming)
Prepare a single PDF or folder with all required materials
Write a scholarship essay (maximum 1,000 words) addressing background, field of study, career goals, interests, community involvement, and academic achievements
Obtain one letter of recommendation written specifically for this scholarship
Assemble a portfolio showcasing relevant work (class projects, designs, marketing audits, writing samples, personal websites, etc.)
Submit the complete application through the Intuitive Digital scholarship portal before the application cap or the August 15th deadline

At Intuitive Digital, we believe marketing’s future should be inclusive, creative, and equitable. That’s why we launched the Inclusion in Digital Marketing Scholarship – a program supporting students from underrepresented communities pursuing careers in digital marketing.

The Lilly Endowment Community Scholarship Program is designed to help raise the level of educational attainment in Indiana, increase awareness of the beneficial roles Indiana community foundations can play in their communities and encourage efforts of Lilly Endowment Community Scholars to engage with each other and with state leaders to improve quality of life in Indiana.
Full-tuition coverage, required fees, and a book stipend for four years.
Does not cover room, board, or travel expenses.
Recipients can attend any accredited public or private four-year college or university in Indiana.
Must be a resident of Indiana.
Must have a high school diploma from an accredited Indiana high school.
Plan to pursue a full-time undergraduate baccalaureate program in Indiana.
Selection criteria and application deadlines vary by county.
Contact your local community foundation for specific selection criteria and application deadlines.
Complete and submit the application, ensuring it aligns with the requirements set by your county's foundation.
Prepare necessary documentation, such as proof of residency and academic records.
Await notification of selection decisions, which are managed locally by Indiana’s community foundations.
Application due dates will vary by county. The earliest deadline is August 15th, in Monroe County. Visit the website to see what the deadline is for your county if you are not in Monroe County.

The DCTAG program team will work with your college or university to cover your tuition expenses if you are eligible for DCTAG funding, and your school is eligible for DCTAG funding. Please note: Students receiving a DCTAG award will not personally receive the funds. The award amount that your college or university will receive from the DCTAG program for your account depends on the type of institution you are attending, the difference between in-state and out-of-state tuition, the academic term, your lifetime maximum award amount (see below), and the amount of federal funding appropriated for the DCTAG program.
Established by Congress through the District of Columbia College Access Act
Administered to assist District of Columbia residents pursuing undergraduate education
Supports attendance at eligible public and private colleges and universities
Recipients currently attend more than 300 participating institutions
Applicants must reapply annually to continue receiving funding
Funding is available only while all eligibility requirements continue to be met
Must be a United States citizen or an eligible non-citizen
Must attend an eligible public or private college or university
Must have established District of Columbia domicile for at least 12 consecutive months before beginning college and maintain residency throughout enrollment
Dependent students under age 24 establish domicile through a parent or legal guardian
Must not be in default on federal student loans
Must possess a high school diploma, GED, National External Diploma Program credential, or equivalent secondary credential
Must have earned the secondary credential within the previous 15 years
Must be enrolled at least half-time in a first undergraduate degree program
Must not already hold a bachelor's degree
Graduate and professional degree students are not eligible
Must maintain satisfactory academic progress as defined by the educational institution
Must meet DCTAG income eligibility requirements
Review the DCTAG eligibility requirements and confirm participation by your intended college or university
Complete the DCTAG application for the applicable academic year
Provide documentation verifying District of Columbia domicile and residency
Submit documentation confirming citizenship or eligible non-citizen status, if required
Provide proof of high school graduation or an eligible secondary credential
Submit any required college admission or enrollment documentation
Complete all required financial and eligibility verification materials before the annual deadline
Reapply each year to maintain eligibility and continued funding

DCTAG was created by Congress in 1999 by the District of Columbia College Access Act; PL 106-98 and amended by DC College Access Improvement Act 2002 and DC College Access Improvement Act 2007 to expand higher education choices for college-bound residents of the District of Columbia. Currently, DCTAG recipients attend more than 300 colleges and universities.
